components.note: 扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.
口 (mouth) — kissing is done with the mouth.
勿 (wù) gives a sound distantly related to wěn, having drifted apart over time.
北 here representing two feet or footprints, one behind the other.
禾 (a stalk of grain), here standing in for a tree or ladder — together depicting someone climbing up, giving 乘 its meaning 'to ride, to get onto.'
宀 (roof) — represents a home.
各 (each, various) — a person arriving from elsewhere and welcomed under one's roof gave 客 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'
辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
介 (jiè) gives a sound hint — 价 is pronounced jià, sharing the same initial consonant though the vowel has shifted.
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
羊 (sheep) — 群 relates to a group or flock, as sheep gather in a flock
君 (jūn) gives a loose sound connection to 群's reading qún
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support
阝 (a mound, a place) — 阴 relates to the shaded side of a hill.
月 (moon) — the moon, associated with night and shade, gave 阴 its meaning 'shady, overcast'; compare 阳, which uses 日 (sun) for the opposite, sunny meaning.
讠 (speech) — 谋 relates to discussing and forming a plan.
某 (mǒu) gives the sound — an exact match with 谋.
忄 (heart) — 慢 describes an unhurried state of mind or pace.
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match with 慢.
忄 (heart) — 慢 describes an unhurried state of mind or pace.
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match with 慢.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'
匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.
走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
二 is simply two horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number two, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 三 (three).
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
心 (heart) — 愿 relates to a heartfelt wish or desire
原 (yuán) gives a loose sound connection to 愿's reading yuàn
子 (child) — 孤 originally described a child without a parent, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) gives a sound close to gū, sharing the same initial.
办 (to manage/handle) — 协 relates to people working together to manage something
十 (shí) gives a sound distantly related to 协's reading xié, having drifted apart over time
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
口 (mouth) — 喉 names a part of the mouth and throat area.
侯 (hóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 喉.
口 (mouth) — 咙 (as in 喉咙) names the throat, an opening in the body.
龙 (lóng) gives the sound — an exact match with 咙's reading.
足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

meanings: to see with one's own eyes

components.note: 目 depicts an eye turned on its side, with the outline and pupil visible — later straightened into today's rectangular shape.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
火 (fire) — flame at the heart of the picture.
暴 (violent, sudden) — a burst of intense fire, together giving 爆 its meaning 'to explode, burst.'
礻 (altar, spirit) on the left sets a religious scene.
兄 (a person, shown here kneeling or speaking) on the right shows someone praying, giving 祝 its meaning 'to wish, to pray for blessings.'
礻 (spirit/altar) — 福 relates to blessings granted by the spirits
畐 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 福's reading fú
氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
冂 (a covering or frame, here representing a cart) — 两 pictures two things sharing one enclosure.
从 (two people following each other) — together with the frame above, 两 shows a pair joined together, giving its meaning 'two' or 'both.'
扌 (hand) — 措 describes arranging or handling something.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to cuò, having drifted apart over time.
囗 depicts an enclosure or fence.
木 (tree) — a tree hemmed in by a fence, unable to grow freely, gave 困 its meaning 'trapped, difficult.'
扌 (hand) — 扰 describes stirring something up by hand, 'to disturb.'
尤 (yóu) is only distantly related in sound to rǎo — the connection has drifted apart over time.
阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'
目 (eye) — 瞄 is an action done with the eyes.
苗 (miáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 瞄.
冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
芒 (the tip of a plant, an awn) — 荒 relates to overgrown, uncultivated land.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to huāng, having drifted apart over time.
广 depicts a roofed building, a school or hall.
肀 depicts a hand holding a writing brush.
口 (mouth) — children reading aloud and writing in school gave 唐 its early meaning, later borrowed as the name of the Tang dynasty.
讠 (speech) — relates to 调's meaning 'to adjust, transfer,' something coordinated through spoken negotiation.
周 (zhōu) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from diào.
敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
宀 (roof) — 审 relates to a formal setting, like a courtroom, where matters are examined
申 (shēn) gives a sound close to 审's reading shěn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
讠 (speech) — 讯 relates to asking questions and gathering information through words.
卂 (xùn) is an exact match for the sound of 讯.
阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn

meanings: junior ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: 少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'
木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
日 (the sun) — sunlight falling over the land
京 (a capital city) — a grand city view worth seeing
A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
忄 (heart) — 惊 relates to an emotional reaction of shock or fright
京 (jīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 惊's reading jīng
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
广 depicts a simple roofed building, a home.
隶 depicts a servant or laborer — a household with help was traditionally a sign of ease and well-being, giving 康 its meaning 'healthy, peaceful.'
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
⺮ (bamboo) — ancient policy documents were written on bamboo strips
朿 (cì) gives a sound distantly related to 策's reading cè, having drifted apart over time
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
宀 (a roof) — a house.
火 (fire) — burning inside it, together giving 灾 its meaning 'disaster, calamity.'
贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi

meanings: to make up for a deficiency

components.note: Bow — original sense of a strung bow, later extended to 'full/filled.'
Gives the sound ěr, related to mí but drifted apart over time.
衤 (cloth) — 补 means to mend or patch clothing.
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 补.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
车 (cart) — the vehicle moving goods.
辶 (walking/movement) — the cart traveling along a road, linking one place to another, giving 连 its meaning 'to connect, link.'
扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
